title: Universal synchronous receiver/transmitter (USRT)

sources.document: Standard Microsystems Corporation 1982 data catalogue, COM2601 Universal Synchronous Receiver/Transmitter
sources.pages: printed 91-94 (PDF pages 92-95): pin configuration, block diagram, description of pin functions

pins.name: VCC
pins.text: +5 V supply

pins.name: TBMT
pins.text: transmitter buffer empty: high when the transmitter data buffer may be loaded with new data

pins.name: TSO
pins.text: transmitter serial output: the whole transmitted character; from the data buffer if TDS was pulsed during the character before, else from the transmitter sync register

pins.name: GND
pins.text: ground

pins.name: SCT
pins.text: sync character transmitted: high when the character loaded into the transmitter shift register came from the transmitter sync register (TDS was not pulsed in time); low when it came from the data buffer

pins.name: VDD
pins.text: -12 V supply

pins.name: DB1
pins.text: data bus input bit 1 (least significant): into the receiver sync register (RSS), the transmitter sync register (TSS) or the transmitter data buffer (TDS)

pins.name: DB2
pins.text: data bus input bit 2: into the receiver sync register (RSS), the transmitter sync register (TSS) or the transmitter data buffer (TDS)

pins.name: DB3
pins.text: data bus input bit 3: into the receiver sync register (RSS), the transmitter sync register (TSS) or the transmitter data buffer (TDS)

pins.name: DB4
pins.text: data bus input bit 4: into the receiver sync register (RSS), the transmitter sync register (TSS) or the transmitter data buffer (TDS)

pins.name: DB5
pins.text: data bus input bit 5: into the receiver sync register (RSS), the transmitter sync register (TSS) or the transmitter data buffer (TDS)

pins.name: DB6
pins.text: data bus input bit 6: into the receiver sync register (RSS), the transmitter sync register (TSS) or the transmitter data buffer (TDS)

pins.name: DB7
pins.text: data bus input bit 7: into the receiver sync register (RSS), the transmitter sync register (TSS) or the transmitter data buffer (TDS)

pins.name: DB8
pins.text: data bus input bit 8: into the receiver sync register (RSS), the transmitter sync register (TSS) or the transmitter data buffer (TDS)

pins.name: RR
pins.text: receiver reset: high resets RDA, SCR, ROR and RPE; the fall from high to low puts the receiver into search mode (sync hunt, bit by bit)

pins.name: RPE
pins.text: receiver parity error: high when the received parity bit does not agree with the selected parity; forced low when NPB is high

pins.name: SCR
pins.text: sync character received: high each time the character loaded into the receiver buffer equals the receiver sync register; low again at the next character that is not

pins.name: TSS
pins.text: transmitter sync strobe: high loads DB1-DB8 into the transmitter sync register

pins.name: TCP
pins.text: transmitter clock: each rising edge shifts one bit out of the transmitter shift register; baud rate = TCP frequency

pins.name: TDS
pins.text: transmitter data strobe: high loads DB1-DB8 into the transmitter data buffer

pins.name: RSS
pins.text: receiver sync strobe: high loads DB1-DB8 into the receiver sync register

pins.name: RSI
pins.text: receiver serial input

pins.name: RCP
pins.text: receiver clock: each falling edge shifts one bit of RSI into the receiver shift register; baud rate = RCP frequency

pins.name: RDAR
pins.text: receiver data available reset: high resets RDA to low

pins.name: RDE
pins.text: received data enable: high enables the outputs RD1-RD8

pins.name: RDA
pins.text: receiver data available: high when a whole character has been received and moved into the receiver buffer register

pins.name: ROR
pins.text: receiver overrun: high if the previous character was not read (RDA not reset) before the present one moved into the receiver buffer

pins.name: RD8
pins.text: received data bit 8; three-state, enabled by RDE; unused bits (by NDB1/NDB2) are low

pins.name: RD7
pins.text: received data bit 7; three-state, enabled by RDE; unused bits (by NDB1/NDB2) are low

pins.name: RD6
pins.text: received data bit 6; three-state, enabled by RDE; unused bits (by NDB1/NDB2) are low

pins.name: RD5
pins.text: received data bit 5; three-state, enabled by RDE; unused bits (by NDB1/NDB2) are low

pins.name: RD4
pins.text: received data bit 4; three-state, enabled by RDE; unused bits (by NDB1/NDB2) are low

pins.name: RD3
pins.text: received data bit 3; three-state, enabled by RDE; unused bits (by NDB1/NDB2) are low

pins.name: RD2
pins.text: received data bit 2; three-state, enabled by RDE; unused bits (by NDB1/NDB2) are low

pins.name: RD1
pins.text: received data bit 1 (least significant, characters are right-justified); three-state, enabled by RDE; unused bits (by NDB1/NDB2) are low

pins.name: NDB2
pins.text: number of data bits, high select bit: NDB2 NDB1 = LL 5, LH 6, HL 7, HH 8 bits per character (taken in by CS)

pins.name: NPB
pins.text: no parity bit: high sends no parity bit, expects none, and forces RPE low (taken in by CS)

pins.name: NDB1
pins.text: number of data bits, low select bit (see NDB2; taken in by CS)

pins.name: CS
pins.text: control strobe: high enters NDB1, NDB2, POE and NPB into the control bits register; may be strobed or wired high

pins.name: POE
pins.text: odd/even parity select with NPB low: low odd parity, high even parity (taken in by CS)

functions.text: Synchronous receiver and transmitter, double buffered. Transmitter: a character written by TDS goes to the data buffer and then to the shift register, shifted out on TSO at each rising TCP; if no character was written in time the transmitter sync register is sent instead (SCT high). Receiver: after RR falls it hunts bit by bit (falling RCP) until the shift register equals the receiver sync register, then loads that character into the receiver buffer and takes every following character (RDA, SCR, ROR, RPE). Word length 5-8 bits and parity set by NDB1, NDB2, NPB, POE through CS.

state.changesOn: TCP rising (transmit), RCP falling (receive), strobes TDS, TSS, RSS, CS, RR, RDAR
rules: RR high resets RDA, SCR, ROR, RPE; RR high-to-low starts the sync search (page 92).
TBMT high: the data buffer may be loaded; SCT high: the last character sent came from the sync register (page 92).
Data bits per character NDB2 NDB1: LL 5, LH 6, HL 7, HH 8 (page 93).
Parity NPB POE: LL odd, LH even, H X none (page 94).

electrical.notes: Datasheet: directly TTL compatible, 250K baud, 200 ns strobes, 300 mW; electrical table pages not transcribed.

unknown: The order in which the bits go out on TSO (LSB first is not stated).
Whether the parity bit takes part in the sync comparison.
The power-on state of the transmitter.
Electrical and timing tables (pages 95-98) not transcribed.
notes: The SMC catalogue names the AMI S2350 as a functional equivalent, but its pin-out differs; nothing from it is used here.

behaviour.reason: The datasheet describes the USRT in words (pin functions, pages 92-94) but not completely: the bit order on the line, whether parity takes part in the sync comparison and the transmitter's power-on state are not stated, so a runnable model cannot be written from it without guessing. The words are in pins[].text and functions.
